newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called $1-$1.50 down, Brent off 10-15c.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called $1-$1.50 down, Brent off 10-15c.

text.p: IPE July gas oil was expected to open on Wednesday down $1-$1.50 a tonne on the back of losses made late on Tuesday on Brent and NYMEX heating oil, brokers said.

Weekly U.S. stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) were seen as neutral to slightly bearish and the market would focus for the day on news from the OPEC meeting in Vienna, they added.
"We may not see large volumes traded but I expect a volatile session which will be rumour led. This market is ready to react to any OPEC headlines," one broker said.
"As every minister says something we'll see a move," he added.

The bearish aspect to the overnight API's was seen in very high refinery runs of 97.6 percent capacity for the second week in a row. The fear that the U.S. market could be flooded with gasoline was tempered by the view that demand has been high enough to prevent that.
In the report U.S. crude stocks fell by 756,000 barrels to 322.3 million with imports down to 8.25 million barrels per day (bpd) from over 10 million bpd in the last report.

Brokers did not see much further downside following Tuesday's news that the Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said his country would start exporting oil again once the aid distribution plan had been finalised in seven to 10 days and that Iraq would start exports at 730,000 to 750,000 bpd.
August Brent was called down 10-15 cents. The contract traded on SIMEX at $17.75 a barrel, down some 12 cents.
